items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: He hired Red Norvo’s quintet, which is pianoless, and added Jack Sheldon and Bill Harris and Flip Phillips.

ctx.x: What about, you’ve been around the world a little bit with some different groups. Do you enjoy traveling like that?

Oh, yeah. I was really fortunate to do some traveling. I know that I could have never done it on my own, to see the variety of stuff and see how people live and how music is different in different places, and the food, and everything is, traveling is one of the greatest things you can do if you do it under good conditions you know. I think my first time was with Benny Goodman in Russia, I mean not in Russia but in Europe in 1959. It was with the small band. He hired Red Norvo’s quintet, which is pianoless, and…
four horns, which made it a ten piece band. And we toured Europe and had a great time. I see more and more stories coming in, as we’re slowing down the interview here.

items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Benny was a great band leader because he’d take whatever band he had and make a show out of it, where this guy would have his number. We had Red Norvo and Jerry Dodgion

ctx.x: We were talking about the vocal thing.

Oh yeah. So we were working in Atlantic City and Flip Phillips and I wrote a song, called “My Baby Done Told Me.” And we had a little arrangement and everything. And it’s recorded on some album — some album made in Europe when we were over there. So I started singing with his band and pretty soon that was part of the show. Benny was a great band leader because he’d take whatever band he had and make a show out of it, where this guy would have his number. We had Red Norvo and Jerry Dodgion and Bill
Harris and Flip Phillips. So it had a lot of little stuff inside the band. We’d have a great little show.
